title: Cambium Fractal Ecosystem — Manifest and Moosh Guide

groups.label: Orient
groups.summary: Understand Cambium as a nested operating system.

groups.label: Resolve
groups.summary: Follow the project-scoped skill cluster and workflow.

groups.label: Govern
groups.summary: Read planning, approval, and safety boundaries.

groups.label: Prove
groups.summary: Separate evidence capture from readiness claims.

chapters.title: Start at the Cambium root
chapters.summary: The project is the root context from which planning, skills, workflows, and evidence are resolved.
chapters.audience: Operators learning the Cambium project model.

evidence.reason: This repository contract does not embed a live still; capture evidence must be supplied by a separately approved bounded run.

body: Cambium is the root scope. Every downstream object must retain project identity before it can be interpreted.
The browser console is a projection of that root, not a substitute for the project contract or an execution worker.
actions: Confirm that the Cambium project is initialized.
Treat the displayed state as observed evidence with a freshness timestamp.

chapters.title: Resolve the product-guides skill lattice
chapters.summary: A cluster hub explains ownership while Moosh spokes provide bounded guide and video capabilities.
chapters.audience: Operators deciding which skill owns the next action.

evidence.description: Manifest workflow projection resolves product-guides to two hubs and two Moosh spokes.

body: The product-guides cluster contains two hubs: the orchestrator routes work and the core defines the shared contract.
The build-product-user-guides spoke owns inventory, still evidence, and guide output. The guide-to-product-video spoke owns motion only after the guide exists.
actions: Read the resolved cluster title and tier.
Identify the hub skills before reading the spokes.
Use the spoke contract only for the stage it owns.

chapters.title: Follow the six workflow stages
chapters.summary: The workflow moves from observation and resolution through guide preparation, evidence, video, and validation.
chapters.audience: Operators planning a safe Moosh run.

evidence.description: The projection reports six ordered stages with read-only, gated, and ready states.

body: Observe-project and resolve-cluster establish context. Prepare-guide and capture-evidence are gated because they touch project evidence.
Compose-video is downstream of guide inventory and a film contract. Validate-report is a read-only proof stage.
actions: Read stages in their reported order.
Separate read-only inspection from evidence-producing work.
Stop at the first unresolved prerequisite.

chapters.title: Read planning and swarm state correctly
chapters.summary: Planning waves and mapped sessions provide coordination evidence, not proof that workers are executing.
chapters.audience: Operators interpreting the project’s planning spine.

evidence.description: The snapshot exposes the observed plan, wave, route, and historical session map.

body: The GSD and next-wave records map intent into waves and tasks. A runtime snapshot may show planning and routing evidence, but that is not a live worker fleet.
A swarm becomes active only through an explicitly authorized dispatch path with its own receipts.
actions: Inspect the plan and wave identifiers.
Do not infer active execution from a mapped session.

chapters.title: Prepare evidence without fabricating it
chapters.summary: Capture is a bounded evidence operation requiring a reviewed configuration, runtime support, and approval.

evidence.description: Capabilities expose project-cwd, Node, Python, Playwright, capture-config, film-spec, provider, and execution gates.

body: The local capture contract is deliberately narrow: one local route, one synthetic persona, a fixed viewport, and a deterministic output directory.
A configuration file is preparation, not evidence. Still and video outputs require their own accepted run receipts.
actions: Review capability state before requesting a run.
Check that routes and personas are synthetic or approved.
Record the resulting evidence artifact and report.

chapters.title: Stop at the approval boundary
chapters.summary: The trigger is request-only and idempotent; it cannot run without a bounded request identifier and existing approval receipt.
chapters.audience: Owners deciding whether to authorize capture.

evidence.reason: This guide carries no live approval state and therefore cannot authorize or submit a trigger request.

body: The default state is GATED until live readback proves the approval receipt and every capability gate reported by the bridge.
A truthful operator explains the next safe action instead of turning a request-only endpoint into implicit execution.
actions: Obtain a bounded approval receipt from the project owner.
Submit only the documented request shape if all gates are resolved.
